title: Kernel safety net and automated rollback playbook
author: Priya Menon
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the safety nets, observability gates, and automated/manual rollback procedures for kernel and runtime patch deployments to Redwood’s serving runtime. It combines release-stage benchmarking gates, profiling hooks, SLO monitoring, and a decision tree for automated rollback and staged remediation. Use this document when rolling out any change that affects GPU kernels, batching paths, KV cache interaction, or kernel scheduling policies.

Why this exists:
- Kernel-level changes can cause fast, system-wide regressions (tail latency, GPU hangs, memory corruption).
- Rolling backwards quickly and predictably limits customer impact and reduces incident scope.
- Provide consistent signals that integrate the benchmarking suite, continuous profiler, and runtime telemetry.

Scope and out-of-band exceptions:
- Applies to all kernel changes merged to the runtime branch and promoted to staging/production clusters.
- Hotfixes that only touch non-execution control-plane code may follow the lighter release checklist, but safety net monitors still apply.
- For air-gapped Private deployments, local operators must run the equivalent benchmarking and profiling steps listed below before approval.

Ownership and contacts:
- Release owner: engineering-release@redwood.com (primary: Priya Menon)
- Kernel SME: Ethan Caldwell
- Runtime SRE oncall: runtime-sre@redwood.com
- Observability/telemetry owner: Marina Lopez
- Escalation path: oncall -> kernel-sme -> eng-manager -> director-of-runtime

Preconditions (gates before canary):
1) Green unit and integration tests for scheduler and kernel modules.
2) Microbenchmarks: no regression > 1.5% in mean latency for core kernels, and no regression > 5% in p95/p99 token throughput on the synthetic-batcher (run locally).
3) Static safety checks: memory boundary sanitizers on in-tree test harness, kernel ABI compatibility checks.
4) CI-generated artifact tagged with build metadata and kernel-compat matrix.

Staging canary process (recommended matrix):
- Canary cohort sizes: 1% -> 5% -> 20% traffic buckets. Advance only after each gate passes for 30 minutes of steady-state and no alerting.
- Run the following in parallel at each step:
  - Canary synthetic smoke run: payloads from the mixed-workload-slo-simulation-suite for 15 minutes.
  - Profiling capture: 30s sampling of kernel traces and NVTX spans, uploaded to the profiling bucket.
  - Benchmark run: run "bench-runner --profile kernel --suite canary-gates" to generate per-kernel latency and occupancy csv.

Release gating thresholds (must be instrumented and evaluated automatically):
- Latency:
  - p50: regression <= 3% vs baseline
  - p95: regression <= 5% vs baseline
  - p99: regression <= 10% vs baseline
- Error budget signals:
  - GPU kernel failure rate (CUDA errors / kernel launches) must be < 0.02% absolute increase
  - RPC retransmits or GRPC error spikes > 3x baseline are blocking
- Resource metrics:
  - GPU memory high watermark increase <= 5% absolute
  - Scheduler pending queue growth: consistent > 10% sustained for > 2m is blocking
- Observability health:
  - Missing KV cache hits or sudden drop in prefix cache hit rate > 7% absolute is blocking

Automated detection rules (implemented in alerting/monitoring):
- alert: KernelLatencyRegression
  expression: increase(runtime_kernel_p99{job="serving",kernel=~".*"}[5m]) > scalar(0.10 * baseline_p99)
  runbook: follow this playbook (section: Automated rollback decision).
- alert: KernelCrashSpike
  expression: increase(runtime_kernel_crash_total[1m]) > 5
- alert: GpuMemoryPressureHigh
  expression: runtime_gpu_memory_utilization > 0.95 for 60s

Automated rollback decision (CI -> staging -> prod CI process integration):
1) If any blocking alert fires during a canary window, the deployment controller will automatically mark the canary as FAILED and initiate a rollback to the previous kernel artifact.
2) The controller will attempt a graceful revert: notify SRE channel, pause further promotions, and schedule a revert job with a 5-minute cooldown.
3) If revert job fails or the cluster is unhealthy, the oncall must escalate to kernel SME for a manual rollback plan (see manual rollback below).

Manual rollback and mitigation steps (ordered):
1) Quarantine the offending cohort: redirect new routing for the canary cohort to fallback model variant and mark cohort draining (API: "redwood-router --drain-cohort <cohort-id>").
2) Execute cluster revert job: "deployctl promote-artifact --to=prod --artifact=<previous-artifact> --reason=kernel-rollback".
3) Run immediate smoke tests:
   - toolchain: "smoke-check --gateway <prod-gateway> --mini-scenarios"
   - confirm p95/p99 latency falls back to baseline within 10 minutes.
4) If smoke tests fail, cut traffic to Dedicated fallback tier and enable read-only mode for high-risk endpoints until further mitigation.

Profiling playbook integration (what to capture and how to interpret):
- Capture points: kernel entry/exit spans, NVTX annotated sections for batch assembly, KV cache stats, GPU utilization counter snapshots.
- Recording commands (example):
  - docker run --rm --privileged profiling-tool --target http://canary-host:8080 --trace 30s --out s3://profiling/canary/<build-id>.tgz
  - nvprof/nvtrace capture for suspect kernel: "nvidia-trace --pid <pid> --duration 20s --output /tmp/trace.nvt"
- Short interpretation checklist:
  1) Is there a measurable shift in kernel occupancy or warp divergence? If yes, suspect kernel code path change.
  2) Are there repeated GPU stalls (SM stalls) co-incident with tail-latency spikes? If yes, verify memory barriers and atomic usage.
  3) Compare sample heatmaps vs baseline using the profiling diff tool: "prof-diff baseline.nvt canary.nvt".

Benchmarking-suite gate (how to run before promotion):
- Command (CI): "bench-suite run --suite=promote-gates --artifact=<build> --compare-to=baseline --report /tmp/report.json"
- Required outputs (CI verifies):
  - per-kernel CSV including mean/p50/p95/p99 and sample count
  - occupancy and concurrency heatmap images
  - end-to-end token throughput measurement with identical synthetic trace input
- Gate pass criteria:
  - No blocking regressions per Release gating thresholds section.
  - Bench variance: coefficient of variation for p95 across 5 runs < 6%

Known failure modes and mitigations (quick reference):
- Symptom: sudden p99 jumps with no increase in qps.
  - Likely causes: kernel codepath regression, memory bank conflicts, or scheduler mis-prioritization.
  - Mitigation: scale canary to 0, capture profiles, and revert.
- Symptom: intermittent GPU watchdog timeouts on certain nodes.
  - Likely causes: driver mismatch or concurrent host process contention.
  - Mitigation: cordon node, repro on a clean node, check driver and CUDA versions.
- Symptom: KV cache miss storms after kernel change.
  - Likely causes: cache invalidation behavior changed or shard affinity drift.
  - Mitigation: temporarily force rewarm on stable kernel or revert; run kv-warmup utility.

Post-incident actions and required artifacts (if rollback happened):
1) Create an incident page in the incident tracker with timeline, build id, and cohort IDs.
2) Attach profiling bundles, bench-suite reports, and alert graphs.
3) Owner (release owner) must schedule a deep dive within 72 hours and assign remediation owners.
4) Update the kernel test harness with a targeted regression test before the next attempt.

Operational runbook snippets (copy/paste safe):
- Promote previous artifact: "deployctl promote-artifact --to=prod --artifact=redwood-runtime-kernel:v1234 --reason=rollback"
- Drain cohort: "redwood-router --drain-cohort canary-2027-02 --timeout 300s"
- Collect profile bundle: "collect-profile --target http://<pod-ip>:9100 --duration 30s --out /tmp/bundle.tgz && aws s3 cp /tmp/bundle.tgz s3://profiling/incident/<incident-id>/bundle.tgz"

Telemetry & dashboards to monitor during rollout (must be on the canary dashboard):
- Kernel p50/p95/p99 by kernel_name and node (timeseries and heatmap)
- GPU error counters (illegal-instruction, illegal-memory-access, oob)
- Scheduler queue length and average wait time
- KV cache hit rate by prefix length and class
- Deploy controller state and promote/rollback events stream

Checklist before reattempting rollout:
- Root cause identified and a test added reproducing regression (unit or benchmark)
- Patch is submitted and reviewed with kernel-SME approval
- Bench-suite baseline updated if change is expected (documented in release notes)
- Canary cohort will be limited in size and have a longer observation window (recommended: 2x)

Release notes guidance (what to record for kernel change):
- Build id, git sha, target kernel modules and API changes
- Bench-suite summary and explicit pass/fail lines for gate metrics
- Profiling bundle id and link to S3
- Known risks and mitigation knobs (e.g., toggle to force old kernel, scheduler flags)

Appendix: quick decision tree (text form)
1) Alert fires during canary -> automated controller attempts revert (wait 5m)
2) Revert succeeded -> run smoke tests, close incident, schedule RCA
3) Revert failed or cluster unhealthy -> escalate to kernel SME, gather profiles, cordon nodes as needed
4) If failure reproducible on single node type -> stop rollout globally and open P0 incident

Related documentation and runbooks:
- See /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/for detailed trace collection and profiler tooling
- See /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/runtime-scaling-experiment-protocol-and-benchmark-checklist-2026 for bench-suite details
- See /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-upgrade-validation-and-canary-matrix-2026 for promotion mechanics

Contact and feedback:
If you find gaps in this playbook or observe a new failure mode, please file an RFC in the runtime team board and tag the owner (Priya Menon).
